item.title: Review: Trump crackdown shatters US hopes for Guatemalans displaced by climate crisis
item.description: As drought worsens, more climate migrants are trekking north – but as US deportations ramp up, rural Guatemalans are running out of options The small plots of farmland in Caparrosa, an Indigenous Maya Ch’orti’ village in eastern Guatemala, are bone dry. It’s mid-June, and the rainy season should have started a month and a half ago, but it’s barely rained at all. The maize is just a few inches tall, and some plots are completely bare. Lidia Molina is nursing her two-and-a-half-year-old daughter, Karla, sitting on a dusty step next to skinny dogs and chickens. “We haven’t planted our maize yet; it’s too dry,” Molina, 30, said. “We’re hoping it will rain soon, or else we’ll have to make do…
